speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: how long have you been experiencing this shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings since your tympanoplasty?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That shooting pain when eating suggests referred pain from the jaw, but could it be related to the surgical site or the ear canal itself? Have you noticed any discharge, swelling, or a feeling of fullness in your right ear recently?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Otoscopic findings are normal, which is reassuring, but the pain when eating suggests possible involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve or a retained foreign body not visible on standard view. Have you experienced any recent headaches, tinnitus, or a sensation of your ear "popping" that might indicate nerve compression or eustachian tube dysfunction? Also, have you noticed any changes in your ear canal skin texture or hearing fluctuation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Gasser's ganglion compression).
